transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you to the clinic today?
Hello. I can’t think straight anymore or make simple decisions at work or school, and it’s starting to scare me. It just feels like my brain is completely foggy all the time now.
Did these thinking problems start after a specific stressful event or major life change, and if so, how long have they been going on?

It started about a year ago when I began juggling full-time shifts at the clinic while starting my nursing classes. A severe staffing shortage hit right around then, which left me working back-to-back shifts with way too much responsibility. I've just felt completely overwhelmed and unable to keep up ever since.
Have you also been feeling excessive worry or anxiety most days about many different things, even when there is no immediate problem?
I don't think it's general anxiety about everything. It's more that my mind just constantly races specifically about the mistakes I've made at work and how far behind I'm falling in school.

Have these concentration and decision-making problems been present continuously for more than 6 months, or did they start within 3 months of the stressful situation and then improve when things got easier?

Yes, they've been going on continuously for over a year now, ever since I started at the clinic and began my classes. They haven't improved at all; in fact, things have only gotten harder and more overwhelming as time has gone on.

Have these symptoms caused you to withdraw from activities or have trouble keeping up with work, school, or relationships, and do they feel clearly tied to the stress of your workload and life changes?

Yes, they have completely disrupted my life; I've fallen behind in my classes, got a formal write-up at the clinic for charting errors, and stopped seeing friends or doing hobbies like jogging. It is absolutely tied to the overwhelming stress of trying to balance my full-time shifts during our staffing shortage with my nursing coursework over this past year.
Have you been feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things most days, or is the main problem the stress and overwhelm from the situation?

It definitely feels like it has turned into something much deeper than just stress. Most days I have this heavy, constant sadness and hopelessness that I just can't shake off. I've also completely lost interest in things I used to love, like jogging and knitting, and now I just lie in bed feeling nothing.

In the past year, have you had most days with depressed mood or loss of interest/pleasure, along with other symptoms like sleep changes, appetite changes, low energy, feelings of worthlessness, or thoughts of death?

Yes, I've been struggling with all of that for over a year now. I barely sleep, have lost so much appetite that my scrubs are hanging off me, and constantly feel like a failure who is moving in slow motion. On my worst nights, it gets so dark that I catch myself wishing I just wouldn't wake up the next morning.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets criteria for a severe depressive episode: persistent depressed mood and marked anhedonia for over a year, with neurovegetative symptoms (insomnia, reduced appetite/weight loss, low energy/psychomotor slowing), feelings of worthlessness/failure, impaired concentration/decision-making, functional impairment at work/school and social withdrawal, and passive death wishes. Although symptoms began in the context of major occupational/school stress, the syndrome is now syndromal and pervasive rather than limited to an adjustment reaction.
